_readme: Answers to the screening questions employers ask on ATS forms.
- Match on the QUESTION TEXT, not on field position. Some ATSs renumber and
reorder fields between postings, and ask location questions twice
with identical wording and two different answers.
- `answer` is what is actually submitted. `match` holds regex-ish phrases
- Anything not in this file is NOT answered automatically. Leave it blank and
surface it to the user - a wrong screening answer is worse than a slow one.
DEMOGRAPHIC QUESTIONS ARE VOLUNTARY. They are voluntary on every form: fill
them only when instructed, and never treat a blank one as an error.
NOT HERE, BY DESIGN: SSN, driver's license, bank details. See profile.json.

contact._comment: Controls contact information fields. Auto-filled by setup.mjs.

email.note: Always this address, never the university one. profile.json carries the university email as UNVERIFIED with an explicit instruction never to type it into a form. Added after external forms stalled on a required 'email *' field with no saved answer.
email.repeat_note: SuccessFactors asks both 'Email Address' and 'Retype Email Address'. repeat:true lets this one answer fill both fields with the identical literal value, which is what a retype box needs - no separate mirrored entry required.

full_name.note: Legal name, per profile.json identity.legal_name. 'preferred name' is answered separately.

phone.note: Same value as profile.json identity.phone. That file is the source of truth.

linkedin.note: Some ATSs show a redirect suffix from the paste. The clean URL above is the one to type.

phonetic_name.note: Typed name as-is rather than a phonetic spelling.

eligibility._comment: Controls work authorization. Auto-filled by setup.mjs.

visa_sponsorship.note: Question asks whether the applicant WILL REQUIRE sponsorship. The answer is No.

age_18_or_older.note: SuccessFactors 'Are you 18 years of age or older?'. Applicant is comfortably over 18.

match: authorized to work in the us
authorized to work in the united states
authorized_to_work_us.note: SuccessFactors 'Are you authorized to work in the US?'. Answer Yes; visa_sponsorship above is separately No (applicant needs no sponsorship).

sourcing._comment: Controls sourcing questions. Needs manual review.

match: how did you hear about this job
how did you hear about this role
how did you originally hear about
how did you hear about us
how_did_you_hear_about_company.note: Reuse 'Website' for the equivalent question at other employers.

answer_options_variant.note: Paylocity offers Online Job Board / Company Website / Friend or Family Member / Other. Pick 'Online Job Board'. The plain-text 'Website' answer above is for free-text or differently-worded versions.

referred_by.note: Nobody refers the applicant; this box is required on Paylocity. Chosen to AGREE with the 'How did you hear about us?' radio directly above it, which is answered 'Online Job Board'. Do not write a person's name here.

match: what was the name of the job board
if you saw this opportunity on another job board
job_board_name.note: Distinct from referred_by ('Online Job Board') - this asks WHICH board.

academic._comment: Controls academic details. Needs manual review.

match: location you would be most interested
preferred_location.note: Asked TWICE with identical wording. The first was a dropdown answered with location 1; the second was a multi-select chip field answered with location 2. If a form asks once, use location 1. If twice, use both in order.

internship_session.note: Time-sensitive. Re-confirm with the applicant once the target session has passed.

preferred_language.note: SuccessFactors 'Preferred Language:' offers 'US English' / 'UK English', NOT plain 'English' - an 'English' answer never start-matched, so the field reverted to '--'. Priority list: the widget picker uses the FIRST entry ('US English', correct for a US applicant); 'English' is kept as the documented fallback for any portal that lists plain 'English'.

account_creation._comment: Controls account creation. Needs manual review.
account_creation._note: SuccessFactors-style portals put up a real account-creation step - Choose Password / Retype Password - before showing the application. FILL_SCREENING never touches a password field unless the matched entry carries allow_password:true - see apply_core.js's CREDENTIAL check.

password.answer: <Choose a password for ATS accounts, 8-18 chars>
password.note: repeat:true so the same literal value fills BOTH 'Choose Password' and 'Retype Password' - a retype box needs an exact mirror, and reusing one entry is simpler and safer than a separate mirrored entry. Meets the stated rule (8-18 chars, upper+lower+digit-or-punct, no spaces/unicode). Scoped narrowly to these two SuccessFactors labels, not the bare word 'password', so it cannot fire on an unrelated portal's login wall.

consent._comment: Controls consent options. Needs manual review.

sms_recruiting.note: Yes by default at EVERY employer, no longer confirm per employer.

match: would you like to opt in to text messages
sms_optin_successfactors.note: SuccessFactors specifically: this exact question is answered No, overriding the general sms_recruiting=Yes rule above. The match phrase here is longer than sms_recruiting's 'text messages' token, so FILL_SCREENING's longest-token ranking picks this entry on this exact wording without editing the general rule.

demographic_voluntary._comment: Controls voluntary demographic details. Needs manual review.
demographic_voluntary._note: VOLUNTARY on every form. Do not fill them without explicit authorization on the run. Ethnicity and Race were ONE entry until recently, which broke on SuccessFactors, which renders Ethnicity and Race as two SEPARATE required dropdowns each needing its own answer. Split below; verified word-for-word against the live picklist options (widgets.js's 'sfpicklist' kind - a custom SF combobox, not a native <select>, so FILL_SCREENING's own select handling never sees these; the `match` arrays below still matter for any OTHER portal that renders these as real <select>/radio fields).

race.note: Added recently - was folded into 'ethnicity' before, which is wrong: SuccessFactors asks Ethnicity and Race as two separate required dropdowns.

disability_status.note: Corrected to match the live SuccessFactors option text exactly ('do not', not "don't"). This is the standard OFCCP/CC-305 self-identification wording, so it should hold on other ATSs too.

employment_history._comment: Controls employment history answers. Needs manual review.
employment_history._note: Answer No to both automatically at ANY employer. Applicant has no prior applications or employment with any current target.

match: have you applied for a job with us before
have you worked with us before
worked_here_before.note: Added 'have you worked for' / 'worked for this company before' for SuccessFactors' exact wording. Answer stays No, consistent with the section _note.

compensation._comment: Controls compensation answers. Auto-filled by setup.mjs.

desired_salary.rule: Low end of the range the posting advertised. Resolved at fill time from the job row's pay column by payLowEnd() in apply_core.js - never hardcoded.
desired_salary.note: Use low end of range as the standing rule. If the posting printed NO rate, PAY_LOW resolves to nothing and the field is left blank rather than guessed.

salary_expectations_open.rule: A plain number, resolved at fill time by parsePageRateLow()/payLowEnd() in apply_core.js - never hardcoded.
salary_expectations_open.note: SuccessFactors 'Salary expectations:' free-text box specifically. It rejects literal text because SF validates this field as numeric. Now resolves to a number: first choice is the LOW end of the posting's own sentence (parsePageRateLow - works across different postings); falls back to the CSV pay column (PAY_LOW's payLowEnd) if the page printed no rate; left blank as a gap if neither has a number. FILL_SCREENING's word-boundary match means the plural 'salary expectations' here does not collide with desired_salary's singular 'salary expectation' token - they never match the same question.

address._comment: Controls address details. Needs manual review.
address._note: From profile.json identity.local_address. Paylocity asks for this on the applicant record AND again, as the EMPLOYER's address, inside every Work History entry - do not confuse the two. avoid_within: these are the applicant's OWN address fields and must never be filled inside a Work History, Education or References block, where an identically-labelled City/County/State/Zip box wants a previous EMPLOYER'S address. Enforced by sectionOf() in FILL_SCREENING.

address_line_2.note: Genuinely empty. Deliberately has no 'match' list so FILL_SCREENING never targets it.

state_province.note: SuccessFactors 'State/Province:' dropdown specifically: lists full state NAMES, not the abbreviation the generic state.answer uses elsewhere. 'state/province' is a longer match token than the generic 'state' entry's, so this wins on that exact label without touching the generic rule.

country.repeat_note: SuccessFactors asks for 'Country' twice - once as 'Country/Region Code:' (phone) and once as 'Country:' (address). Both want the same answer, so repeat:true lets this one entry fill both instead of the second being starved because the first already consumed it.

county.note: This is the applicant's own county - an employer's county is a different field.

availability._comment: Controls availability fields. Auto-filled by setup.mjs.

start_date.rule: Write the date of the day the application is actually submitted, formatted to whatever the field asks. DO NOT assume MM/DD/YYYY: some ATSs store ISO format, and others want text. Read the field's existing/placeholder format first.
start_date.note: Just write the date of day that the application is sent. Never a hardcoded date - compute it at fill time.

hours_preference.note: Agrees with the part-time-only hard rule in lib.js (FULLTIME_RE). Where a portal offers a set of hour bands, pick the part-time one; never tick a full-time band.

identity._comment: Controls personal identity choices. Auto-filled by setup.mjs.

pronouns.note: Voluntary on most portals; answer it when asked.

certifications._note: These are the qualifications that make the candidate a strong applicant, so fill them whenever asked.

certification_1.note: This is the certification's NAME. If a certificate ID is ever needed, ask the applicant; do not invent one.

certification_2.rule: Reformat to whatever the field wants. Some ATSs take text format; others want MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD. Stored ISO so it can be reformatted.

employer_address._comment: Controls previous employer address. Needs manual review.
employer_address._note: Addresses of PREVIOUS EMPLOYERS, for the work-history blocks on application forms. Double-guarded: Work History section AND a block naming that employer. Never confuse these with the address.* group, which is the applicant's own home address and is barred from these same sections.

reston_street.note: Paylocity's resume parser prefills this box with a city, not a street. Correct it by hand if needed.

reston_county.note: This is the employer's county - NOT the applicant's own county.

education._comment: Controls education details. Needs manual review.
education._note: From profile.json academic{}: University, major, academic level, expected graduation. Do NOT write alternate generic names if the major has a specific name.

application_terms._comment: Controls terms acceptance checkboxes. Needs manual review.

i_accept.note: Authorises checking SuccessFactors Applicant Acknowledgement checkbox - attesting the application info is true and complete - on every application. FILL_SCREENING's checkbox handling treats a truthy answer (true/yes/accept/check/agree) as 'check this box'; it never unchecks anything.
